threat_event: Attacker uses an OEM direct VPN to a plant OT firewall (Pine Hollow governors or Sawgrass Run turbine controls) to reach the OT WAN and command spillway gates or units
threat_source: Nation-state or criminal group targeting dams; compromised OEM support account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Two always-on OEM VPNs bypass the jump hosts, with no MFA, recording, or log review; flat OT WAN lets a plant connection reach gate controllers at all 4 dams
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a access control; Form 3 Q12a-12c); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 6); C-DAMS-R02 (12.3(b)(4)(ii), (xi))
existing_controls: Interim from 2026-09-15: OEM VPNs disabled except during approved sessions opened by the ROC shift supervisor; gate PLCs hold position on loss of communication; local control at every gate
treatment_plan: Move both OEMs to the jump hosts with MFA, recording, and weekly log review; remove the direct VPN profiles; contract security terms for both OEMs
exposure_estimate_usd: $5M-$50M+ (uncontrolled release toward BWB inundation zone of about 38,000; liability; FERC action)

threat_event: Attacker at an RMOS client site moves through the client tunnel into the ROC SCADA zone and operates company gates and units
threat_source: Criminal or nation-state actor compromising a smaller client licensee
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: RMOS client tunnels terminate in the same ROC SCADA zone that controls company gates; client security unknown; no interconnection terms
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation; FAQ Q10 interconnection)
existing_controls: Site-to-site tunnels with certificates; client SCADA objects grouped by client
treatment_plan: Separate RMOS zone at the ROC that can reach only client SCADA objects; per-client firewall rules; client security schedule with incident notice
exposure_estimate_usd: $5M-$50M+ (same consequence as R-001, entered through a client)

threat_event: Ransomware encrypts corporate IT and steals RMOS client data, forcing the company to separate IT from OT
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Large corporate footprint (940 devices); IdP is also the jump host MFA source; no crisis plan for forced IT/OT separation; client data in the portal and file shares
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a intrusion detection and response); Fla. Stat. 501.171 (employee data)
existing_controls: MFA for all users; EDR with 24x7 MSSP; immutable cloud backups; OT firewalls deny corporate traffic except to the jump hosts
treatment_plan: Ransomware crisis plan with a pre-approved IT/OT separation procedure; break-glass jump host MFA; client notice terms; executive tabletop
exposure_estimate_usd: $2M-$8M (outage, forensics, client notices and credits, lost field services revenue; insurance limit $15M)

threat_event: Attacker on a Pine Hollow or Sawgrass Run host moves across the flat OT WAN to controllers at Blackwater Bend and Cedar Shoals
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT WAN routed flat between sites; no OT monitoring at CDS, PNH, or SGR
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation; Form 3 Q11, Q22); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1)
existing_controls: Site OT firewalls at the corporate boundary; local control at every site
treatment_plan: Per-site OT zones with conduits through site firewalls; allow only ROC-to-site SCADA flows

threat_event: Malware exploits one of the 9 unsupported Windows OT hosts at Pine Hollow or Sawgrass Run
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Unsupported operating systems; no patch cadence; legacy antivirus with stale signatures
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a system lifecycle (patching); Table 9.3b vulnerability assessment)
existing_controls: Plant OT firewalls; hosts not reachable from corporate except through jump hosts
treatment_plan: Replace the 9 hosts; EDR or allowlisting on the rest; quarterly patch cadence after vendor qualification

threat_event: Unauthorized or mistaken gate or unit command at Pine Hollow or Sawgrass Run cannot be traced to a person
threat_source: Insider error or misuse; outsider with a shared password
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared operator accounts on PNH and SGR plant HMIs; passwords not changed at departures
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3b access control); C-DAMS-R02 (12.10(a)(2) (causes of the condition))
existing_controls: Card-access control rooms; SCADA journal at the ROC
treatment_plan: Named HMI accounts at PNH and SGR; password change at every departure until then

threat_event: An intrusion at Cedar Shoals, Pine Hollow, or Sawgrass Run goes undetected for weeks
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No OT network monitoring at 3 of 4 projects; plant HMI logs not collected
existing_controls: OT sensors and MSSP at the ROC and BWB
treatment_plan: Passive OT sensors and log collection at CDS, PNH, and SGR with MSSP alerting

threat_event: A cyber event corrupts PLC, governor, or HMI configurations at Cedar Shoals, Pine Hollow, or Sawgrass Run, or the ROC SCADA, and they cannot be restored within the BIA RTO
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Configuration backups incomplete for 3 plants; 5 governor settings only at the OEMs; ROC SCADA cyber recovery not planned; restore tested only at BWB
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A 7.4.2; Table 9.3a restoration and recovery; Form 3 Q16)
existing_controls: BWB restore test 2025; monthly backups at ROC and BWB; local control
treatment_plan: Complete and verify backups at all plants; obtain the 5 governor settings; annual restore test per plant; ROC SCADA cyber recovery in the Rapid Recovery sub-element
exposure_estimate_usd: $1M-$5M (weeks of local operation and lost generation)

threat_event: An attacker in the SCADA domain disables both the primary and backup ROC
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Backup ROC shares the SCADA domain and the flat OT WAN; no isolated recovery environment
existing_controls: Local control at every site; 24x7 BWB staffing
treatment_plan: Isolated recovery environment at the backup ROC with offline images; separate credentials for the standby

threat_event: During recovery, the PNH or SGR governor OEM cannot supply settings or support quickly
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Governor settings for 5 units held only by the OEMs; no contract recovery terms
existing_controls: OEM support contracts (business hours)
treatment_plan: Obtain and escrow the 5 settings files; recovery support terms in renewals

threat_event: FERC finds Section 9 non-compliance and the annual certification letters inaccurate, and issues a directive
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Section 9 not re-evaluated in 2024 or 2025; RMOS and SGR interconnections omitted; asset inventory incomplete
existing_controls: Re-determination done 2026-07-16; plan and schedule sent 2026-09-30
treatment_plan: Annual Section 9 re-evaluation in the compliance calendar; complete inventory; accurate 2026 certification letter

threat_event: The Regional Entity finds the CIP-003-9 Section 6.3 requirement unmet for vendor remote access at Cedar Shoals
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No method to detect malicious communications in vendor sessions at CDS since 2026-04-01
existing_controls: Jump host recording at CDS; session approval
treatment_plan: Extend jump host session inspection to CDS; General Counsel decides self-report by 2026-10-15
exposure_estimate_usd: Penalty range not estimated (Regional Entity discretion)

threat_event: The CIP-012 plan lacks methods for loss and recovery of the ICCP link required since 2026-07-01
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2022 plan written for CIP-012-1
existing_controls: Encrypted ICCP; BA/TOP voice backup in practice
treatment_plan: Update the plan with alternate path and recovery methods agreed with the BA/TOP; self-report decision

threat_event: The single leased ICCP circuit fails and the BA/TOP loses real-time data from BWB and CDS
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One circuit, no diverse path
existing_controls: Voice updates; carrier repair SLA
treatment_plan: Second path over the company microwave to a BA/TOP backup point

threat_event: A cyber event affecting gates or units is not reported to the Regional Engineer as a condition affecting project safety
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: IR plan does not link cyber events to 18 CFR 12.10 or the EAPs
existing_controls: Chief Dam Safety Engineer reports physical conditions reliably
treatment_plan: POL-03 and P08 decision step for 12.10 within the first hours; train shift supervisors

threat_event: After a cyber-caused release, EAP notifications start late because operators are unsure whether a cyber event is an emergency
threat_source: Internal process gap during an attack
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No cyber triggers in the EAPs or the Internal Emergency Response sub-elements
existing_controls: Annual EAP readiness tests; siren tests
treatment_plan: Cyber triggers in all 4 EAP flowcharts and Security Plans; joint cyber and EAP exercise with county emergency management

threat_event: Manipulated instrument data hides a developing failure mode (for example rising piezometric levels) from dam safety staff
threat_source: Sophisticated adversary with access to data acquisition units
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Data acquisition units at CDS, PNH, SGR unmonitored; no integrity checks on instrument data
existing_controls: Manual readings of critical instruments; independent visual inspections
treatment_plan: Signed data from loggers where supported; manual cross-check of critical instruments weekly

threat_event: During a flood that forces all-local operation at night, the company cannot staff all 20 gate panels with qualified operators
threat_source: Hurricane season flood combined with a SCADA or network outage
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 22 qualified call-out gate operators for 20 panels at 4 dams (P05 finding 3)
existing_controls: Annual local operation drills; standby generators
treatment_plan: Cross-train 12 more plant staff; pre-stage crews before forecast floods

threat_event: An intruder enters a spillway gate house and tampers with a local gate panel
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Remote gate houses at PNH and SGR rely on locks and alarms; response time up to 45 minutes
existing_controls: Locks, intrusion alarms, cameras, patrols
treatment_plan: Tamper switches on panel enclosures at PNH and SGR wired to the security desk

threat_event: A disgruntled operator or engineer deliberately misoperates gates or units
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Broad operator rights; no insider threat program
existing_controls: Background checks; SCADA journal at the ROC; two-person rule for logic changes
treatment_plan: Insider threat awareness; alerts on unusual gate commands; HR and security referral process

threat_event: Phishing steals an engineer corporate session and the attacker reaches the jump hosts through MFA fatigue
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Push MFA; jump host access tied to corporate identity
existing_controls: Number matching; conditional access; session approval by the ROC shift supervisor
treatment_plan: Phishing-resistant keys for the 40 jump host users

threat_event: A compromised OEM or SCADA vendor pushes a malicious update or session into plant controls
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No supplier assessments for OEMs; no integrity checks on vendor files at PNH and SGR
existing_controls: SCADA vendor test system at the ROC; change board
treatment_plan: Vendor tiering and assessments; hash verification of vendor files; test before deployment for all plants

threat_event: An OT vendor has an incident but does not tell the company in time
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 9 of 14 OT vendor contracts have no security or notice terms
existing_controls: Informal relationships with OEM account managers
treatment_plan: Security schedule with 24-hour incident notice in all OT vendor contracts at renewal or by amendment

threat_event: After an incident at or through a client site, the company and a client dispute who was responsible
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: RMOS client contracts define no security responsibilities or incident notice; 2 operating orders lack handback times
existing_controls: Operating orders for 4 operated projects
treatment_plan: Client security schedule (responsibilities, notice within 24 hours, handback within 4 hours) in all contracts at the 2027 renewals

threat_event: The company cannot deliver a SOC 2 Type 2 report by the 2027 renewals and loses RMOS clients
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Controls not yet operating consistently; observation period not started
existing_controls: P09 readiness plan; budget approved
treatment_plan: Type 1 by 2027-03-31; Type 2 observation 2027-04-01 to 2027-09-30
exposure_estimate_usd: Up to $11.5M a year of RMOS revenue

threat_event: CEII (EAP inundation maps, design drawings) leaks from engineering shares or the data lake and helps someone plan an attack
threat_source: Insider or outsider with corporate access
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: About 400 users can open inundation maps and drawings; data lake copies unclassified
regulatory_driver: CEII, 18 CFR 388.113(c)(2); C-DAMS-R01 (Form 1 Q22; Rev. 3A 3.2 OPSEC)
existing_controls: Restricted library for Security Program documents; confidentiality agreements
treatment_plan: Move maps and drawings into the restricted library with named access; classify data lake datasets; download alerts

threat_event: The identity provider is down or compromised during an OT incident, removing jump host MFA and remote support
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Jump host MFA depends on the corporate identity provider
existing_controls: On-site staff can operate without remote access
treatment_plan: Break-glass MFA for jump hosts independent of the corporate identity provider

threat_event: Default credentials on river gauge modems or a gate panel modem are used to falsify gauge data or reach a PLC
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 3 of 9 gauge modems and the SGR panel modem had default passwords (P07)
existing_controls: Private APN for gauges; SGR modem disconnected 2026-08-13
treatment_plan: Change all device passwords; remove the SGR modem; device credential check in the inventory

threat_event: Malware enters plant controls through removable media or a vendor laptop at Pine Hollow or Sawgrass Run
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No media kiosks or transient asset checks at PNH and SGR
existing_controls: Kiosks at the ROC and BWB
treatment_plan: Media kiosks and transient asset checks at all plants

threat_event: A field services laptop carries malware into a client dam control system
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Company laptops connect to client equipment; no OT-specific laptop build
existing_controls: EDR on laptops; client supervision
treatment_plan: Dedicated hardened field engineering laptops scanned before each client visit

threat_event: Business email compromise diverts a vendor or settlement payment
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Payment changes approved by email
existing_controls: MFA; email filtering; awareness training
treatment_plan: Call-back verification for bank detail changes; finance-specific training

threat_event: Employee personal information is stolen from the HR or payroll SaaS
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SaaS accounts protected by MFA; vendor security reviewed only at onboarding
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171; other states where employees reside
existing_controls: MFA; vendor SOC 2
treatment_plan: Annual Tier 1 SOC 2 review of HR and payroll vendors (P09)

threat_event: A misconfigured storage location in the OT data account exposes instrument data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Rapid growth of analytics datasets
existing_controls: Guardrails deny public storage; posture alerts
treatment_plan: Classification tags and data-access logging

threat_event: A portal defect shows one RMOS client data from another client
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Multi-tenant portal; no penetration test yet
existing_controls: Tenant tests at each release; code review
treatment_plan: Penetration test before the SOC 2 observation period

threat_event: Dam safety staff rely on AI-001 and miss a developing anomaly the model did not flag
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No validation, version control, or monitoring rules for AI-001 (gap 12)
existing_controls: Manual trend reviews and trigger-point checks unchanged
treatment_plan: P10 conditions: validation, registry, monitoring, no reduction in manual review

threat_event: AI-002 underestimates inflow before a storm and pre-release starts late
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No forecast skill tracking; model used in daily operating decisions
existing_controls: Operators also use public river forecasts; reservoir rule curves
treatment_plan: Forecast skill monitoring; public forecast shown alongside; operator override rule (P10)

threat_event: Staff paste CEII or control details into the enterprise generative AI assistant or a public chatbot
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: AI-005 rolled out without an AI policy
existing_controls: Enterprise assistant contract excludes training on company data
treatment_plan: AI policy; restricted library excluded from the assistant; public chatbots blocked

threat_event: AI-003 video analytics miss a person at a spillway gate house
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Night and rain performance not measured
existing_controls: Intrusion alarms; patrols
treatment_plan: Quarterly detection tests at night and in rain

threat_event: A hurricane cuts power and communications at several projects at once
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Projects within the same storm track; microwave towers exposed to wind
existing_controls: Standby generators; satellite phones at the ROC and BWB; pre-storm staffing plan
treatment_plan: Satellite phones at CDS, PNH, and SGR; generator fuel for 7 days

threat_event: An OEM changes plant logic over a direct VPN without the change board and causes a misoperation
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OEM changes bypass change control at PNH and SGR
existing_controls: Change board at the ROC and BWB
treatment_plan: All vendor changes through the jump hosts and change board with security review

threat_event: Other undocumented remote connections like the Sawgrass Run modem exist at plants not yet inventoried
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT inventory complete only for the ROC and BWB; modem found during P07
existing_controls: Walkdowns at CDS, PNH, and SGR scheduled
treatment_plan: Physical walkdown of every panel at CDS, PNH, and SGR; cellular signal survey; passive monitoring

threat_event: Licensed microwave links are jammed and the ROC loses contact with a project
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Microwave is the backup path; fiber cut and jamming together are unlikely
existing_controls: Fiber primary; local control
treatment_plan: Accepted: local control covers the outage; reviewed annually

threat_event: The MSSP misses or delays an OT alert from the ROC or BWB sensors
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSSP analysts have limited OT knowledge
existing_controls: Monthly service reviews; escalation SLA
treatment_plan: OT playbooks for the MSSP; quarterly test alerts

threat_event: Shared local administrator passwords on OT Windows hosts are reused to move between hosts
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Local admin passwords shared within controls engineering; rotated twice a year
existing_controls: Jump hosts with MFA
treatment_plan: Unique local administrator passwords with a vault; privileged access management for OT administrators

threat_event: A former employee uses SCADA access that was not removed on time
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 3 of 25 sampled leavers kept SCADA domain access 9 to 40 days (P07)
existing_controls: Remote access requires MFA through the corporate IdP, which is disabled at termination
treatment_plan: HR termination feed to the SCADA domain; weekly reconciliation

threat_event: A ransom is paid to a sanctioned party
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Pressure to restore quickly
existing_controls: POL-03 requires OFAC check, counsel, and CEO approval before any payment
treatment_plan: Accepted: policy control is sufficient; reviewed annually

threat_event: A denial-of-service attack takes the RMOS portal offline
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Internet-facing portal
existing_controls: Provider DDoS protection; WAF; 72-hour MTD
treatment_plan: Accepted: provider protection and the 72-hour MTD cover the impact

threat_event: Loss of key controls engineers leaves plant systems understood only by the OEMs
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Knowledge concentrated in a few engineers and OEMs
existing_controls: 24 controls engineering and I&C staff
treatment_plan: Documented procedures for each plant; cross-training

threat_event: GPS time signals are spoofed and log timestamps drift
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: GPS time sources at each site
existing_controls: SIEM normalizes time; protection systems do not depend on GPS time
treatment_plan: Accepted: low impact on safety; reviewed annually

threat_event: An undetected cyber action at Blackwater Bend causes a release that also endangers Cedar Shoals, 22 river miles downstream
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Cascade between company dams; EAPs do not model a cyber-caused cascade
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.1b item 5 (cascading actions); Rev. 3A 4.2 (other dam owners))
existing_controls: BWB staffed 24x7; CDS reservoir rule curve
treatment_plan: Add the cascade scenario to the Vulnerability Assessment update and both EAP exercises

threat_event: Undetected flows draw the Cedar Shoals reservoir below the county water intake
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: CDS has no OT monitoring; reservoir alarms only in SCADA
existing_controls: Staff gauge readings; county intake alarms
treatment_plan: Independent reservoir level alarm to the county water plant over a separate network
